Case Name: Load shell and show login card without a session
Precondition:
1. openan-portal is deployed behind its own nginx entry (container port 8080) and reaches the deployed orchestration-center through BACKEND_URL
2. orchestration-center access authentication is active (its user store holds the built-in admin account, or access_password is set in file mode)
3. The browser context holds no session_token cookie and no localStorage entry for the portal origin
4. The Playwright context sets i18nextLng=en in localStorage before the first navigation
Steps:
1. Open http://<PORTAL_HOST>:8080/ and wait until the login card is visible see result 1
2. Capture the response of GET /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/check issued during boot see result 2
3. Assert the login card controls and the absence of the shell navigation see result 3
4. Cleanup: clear cookies and localStorage for the origin, reload the page and re-check the session see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The document returns 200 with content-type text/html, the title is "OpenAN Portal" and the #root element is populated
2. HTTP 200 with data.auth_required=true and data.authenticated=false
3. The username input (autocomplete=username), the password input and the submit button labelled "Enter" are visible; no header navigation element is rendered and no plugin route container is mounted in the main area (the auth gate returns before routing, so no plugin page can be on screen)
4. After the reload the login card is shown again and GET /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/check returns data.authenticated=false, so the case left no session behind

3. All enabled entries of portal/bundled-plugins.json have their artifacts installed under the portal public /plugins/<id>/

Expected Result:
1. POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/login returns 200 with data.username=admin and data.role=admin, and sets an HttpOnly session_token cookie
2. The header navigation is rendered with the manifest-driven buttons (the Registry Center and Orchestration Center buttons and the AN Ontology group button are visible) and the login card is no longer in the DOM; nav ordering is asserted only by FIT-openan-portal-plugin-registry-002

Case Name: Refuse to restore protected routes after the session is revoked
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. The test can issue a request that does not share the browser cookie jar (a separate Playwright APIRequestContext)
3. The registry-center bundle is enabled, so /registry is a protected route behind the shell
Steps:
1. Sign in as admin and record the session_token cookie and the auth/check payload see result 1
2. Revoke the same session server-side with POST .../auth/logout sent from the out-of-band context with the captured token as a Bearer credential see result 2
3. Without reloading, open /users so the shell issues a host-scope API call see result 3
4. Reload the page and request /registry directly see result 4
5. Cleanup: clear the stale cookie, reload and re-check the session see result 5
Expected Result:
1. GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=true with data.role=admin and the session_token cookie is present in the browser context
2. The logout returns 200 and the browser still holds the same session_token cookie, because the Set-Cookie of that response never reached the browser context; GET .../auth/check with the same cookie now returns data.authenticated=false
3. GET .../auth/users returns 401, the axios interceptor dispatches auth-expired, the login card replaces the shell and location.pathname stays /users, so the stale session is dropped without a manual reload
4. The login card is shown at /registry, GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=false and no /api/registry-center request is issued, so the revoked session cannot be restored by navigation
5. The cookies are cleared, the reload shows the login card and GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=false, so the case left no session behind

Case Name: Keep the shell authenticated when a sub-app returns 500 or times out
Precondition:
1. openan-portal, registry-center and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. The registry-center bundle declares backend.gateway /api/registry-center without authScope (component scope); the orchestration-center bundle declares no backend.gateway, so its requests use the shell client
3. The Playwright context can intercept /api/registry-center/** and /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows
Steps:
1. Sign in, open /registry, intercept /api/registry-center/** to answer 500 and reload the route see result 1
2. Assert the host authentication state and the shell chrome after the component failure see result 2
3. Replace the interception with an aborted /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows request and open /orchestration see result 3
4. Request /registry again while the failure injection is still in place and assert the host session see result 4
5. Cleanup: remove the interceptions, reload /registry and re-assert the data path see result 5
Expected Result:
1. location.pathname stays /registry, the registry sub-app renders its own toast with the registry-center toast.load_failed text (Failed to load agents.) and the header still shows the Logout button; no login card, no role=alert banner and no "Plugin Error" boundary text
2. GET .../auth/check still returns data.authenticated=true, the session_token cookie is unchanged and no auth-expired redirect happened, because a component-scope error is rejected without dispatching the auth-expired event
3. location.pathname equals /orchestration, the workflows request fails as a network error (the route was aborted, which is how the client timeout path surfaces) and the nav plus Logout are still rendered with no login card
4. location.pathname equals /registry, agent-cards/manage returns 200 (the timeout in the other sub-app did not affect this one), GET .../auth/check still returns data.authenticated=true and the nav still renders all 8 manifest entries
5. GET /api/registry-center/rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards/manage returns 200 again, the role=alert count is 0 and the agent list is rendered
